newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech FinMin mulls budget spending cuts - agency.
newsitem.headline: Czech FinMin mulls budget spending cuts - agency.

text.p: The Czech Fiannce Ministry is preparing a series of state budget spending cuts in order to keep the 1997 budget in balance, the local news agency CTK said on Thursday.
It quoted Deputy Finance Minister Miroslav Havel as saying that the proposal on cuts would be submitted to the government.
"We are preparing a package of measures... which will mean a certain restrictive action on the expenditure side of the state budget," CTK quoted Havel as saying.

CTK said Havel did not elaborate on the extent of the proposed cuts nor when the proposal would be presented to the full cabinet. Ministry officials were not immediately available for further comment.

The parliament approved the 1997 budget as balanced with both revenues and expenditures standing at 549.1 billion crowns, but the state account showed a deficit of 6.7 billion crowns at the end of February, amid signs of a slowdown in economic growth.
Last year's budget ended with a small deficit of 1.56 billion after a series of spending cuts at the end of the year.
At end-February 1996, the budget was in surplus by 3.2 billion crowns.

The centre-right coalition government, which had made balanced state finances a cornerstone of its policy, had managed to keep the budget in surplus since 1993 to 1995, in the first three years of the Czech Republic's existence.
